feedback: The investigation flow worked well. The tools correctly identified frontend as the error origin. The main challenge was the change attribution — both frontend changes were flagged as non-culprits by investigate_change because the diff_touches ("layout") didn't semantically match tcp.connect errors. In practice, a frontend deploy touching "layout" could absolutely reconfigure service mesh settings, gRPC stubs, or environment variables that affect connectivity. The investigate_change tool was too literal in its content matching. The timing + service correlation (only pre-onset change on the faulting service) is the stronger signal here. The correlate_attribute_fault tool's service vs edge classification was debatable — frontend server spans error because the handler fails, but the underlying issue is connectivity to recommendation. The tool chose "service" which seems right since the fault is in frontend's own deployment.
